background_loops_changed: services/telemetry_sharing_service.py::TelemetrySharingService (wake/tick split; dueness from the persisted stamp; fresh SingleFlightLock per claim, released only when the receiver did not acknowledge; persisted retry cap; fenced stamp write; lifespan stop hook in main.py)
tests: tests/unit/test_2618_heartbeat_dueness.py (36 tests; fake settings store, fake httpx, fakeredis marker, patched clock)

hardening_shipped: share_now's True now means 'the receiver acknowledged': the post-2xx stamp write is fenced, so a local write failure can no longer be reported as a failed send — under the new release-on-failure path an unfenced write would have re-sent an accepted snapshot every wake on both workers
the cross-worker marker is constructed per claim (SingleFlightLock is single-use) and only the lock created in the current tick can be released, so a fail-open claim can never delete a live marker
attempt frequency during a receiver outage is capped from the persisted send log (five consecutive failures, then one attempt per half-interval) — bounded without Redis and restart-proof
the heartbeat is stopped in lifespan shutdown and a cancellation mid-send releases the marker, so a dead process's marker cannot block the next boot's first wake
egress CONDITIONS are unchanged: the config kill switch and the stored consent are evaluated before any stamp read or Redis touch; a settings read failure reads as consent-off
the one new WARNING and the loop guard log a period, a count or an exception class only — never TELEMETRY_SHARING_URL, which is operator-supplied and may carry userinfo

supply_chain_summary.node: no dependency files changed (a pnpm lockfile created by the host vitest run was deleted, never staged)

notes: EXCLUDED (rule 1, DoS / rate limiting): the wake changes ATTEMPT frequency during a receiver outage or on an air-gapped consented install (from one per day to at most one per wake for the first five failures, then one per half-interval); the diff itself adds the cap, and content, gates and recipient are unchanged

EXCLUDED (rule 5, hardening without a concrete vulnerability): the documented reset path `DELETE /api/settings/telemetry_sharing_last_shared_at` (admin-gated, human-only) now yields one heartbeat within 10–20 minutes instead of at the next boot-relative tick; consent still gates, the document is the same anonymized aggregate, and the change is documented in the feature flow and FR-7

EXCLUDED (rule 6, race not concretely exploitable): `release_if_owned` is GET-then-DELETE (the pre-existing primitive, compare-and-delete on the caller's own token); the only writers are trusted backend workers and agents cannot reach Redis (two-network invariant #589), so no attacker-controlled interleaving exists

CHECKED, not a finding: the `_loop` guard's `logger.exception` — every callee on the guarded path (`_read`, `is_consent_enabled`, `_recent_sends`, `_claim_tick`, `share_now`) swallows its own errors and none holds the URL or a credential in scope, so a traceback there could only come from a programming error in the pure helpers

trend.note: diff-mode reports are branch-scoped; the ent#190 report covered the same module's benchmark read and also closed with no findings — no fingerprint overlap
